\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{کم} \ur{کرنا} (kam karnā)}{کم کرنا (kam karnā)}]{\ur{کم} \ur{کرنا} (kam karnā) — to reduce}

\label{lesson:UR-C215-kam-karna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to earn, then the Urdu for to look after.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{کم} \ur{کرنا}}
\textbf{\ur{کم} \ur{کرنا}} — \emph{kam karnā} — \textquotedblleft{}to reduce\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{کم} \ur{کرنا}} (\emph{kam karnā}) is \textquotedblleft{}to make less\textquotedblright{}. \emph{kam}, \textquotedblleft{}little, less\textquotedblright{}, is usually traced to Persian \emph{kam}; \emph{karnā} comes from Sanskrit \emph{karoti}, \textquotedblleft{}does\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 2814).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for this chapter.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kam karnā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kam karnā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{kam karnā}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for to earn, then the Urdu for to look after, then say \emph{kam karnā} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{پیچھا} \ur{کرنا} (pīchhā karnā)}{پیچھا کرنا (pīchhā karnā)}]{\ur{پیچھا} \ur{کرنا} (pīchhā karnā) — to chase}

\label{lesson:UR-C215-pichha-karna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to look after, then the Urdu for to reduce.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{پیچھا} \ur{کرنا}}
\textbf{\ur{پیچھا} \ur{کرنا}} — \emph{pīchhā karnā} — \textquotedblleft{}to chase\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{پیچھا} \ur{کرنا}} (\emph{pīchhā karnā}) is \textquotedblleft{}to do the rear\textquotedblright{}, to follow behind. CDIAL lists \emph{pīchā}, \textquotedblleft{}rear\textquotedblright{}, under a reconstructed \emph{*paśca}, \textquotedblleft{}hinder part\textquotedblright{}, taken from Sanskrit \emph{paścāt}, \textquotedblleft{}behind\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 7990). \emph{karnā} comes from Sanskrit \emph{karoti}, \textquotedblleft{}does\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 2814).
\end{cousinweb}
